run.question:
Our US prod cluster is having a checkout incident — investigate using
app-262-prod-logs.

report.summary: The index app-262-prod-logs contains exactly 5 documents, and only 3 of them are errors: they belong to cluster production-us-east-1 (the US prod cluster the question names) and describe a payment-provider timeout chain at 2026-11-23T15:32:53Z–17:02:53Z. checkout-service logged 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (Stripe-US)', payment-service logged 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms', and checkout-service then logged 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 44%)'. The only non-error records in the index carry cluster production-eu-west-1 (healthy checkout at 16:32:53Z and 17:02:53Z) and therefore say nothing about the US cluster. So the supported reading is that the US-prod checkout incident is driven by timeouts to the external payment provider named stripe-us, with checkout's payment-service circuit breaker opening as the consequence; the deepest evidence ends at that external provider, which is not a Kubernetes object and which I could not inspect. Kubernetes access in this Run is to cluster `production`, a different cluster from production-us-east-1: there every otel-demo pod (including checkout-6578865d87-v6flf and payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm) is Running/Ready with 0 restarts, payment/checkout Services have endpoints, no NetworkPolicy or ResourceQuota exists, and the flagd fault-injection flags (paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable) all have defaultVariant 'off' with the flagd-config ConfigMap applied once by helm at 14:36:29Z — so pod-level, service-level and feature-flag explanations are not supported for that cluster, and remain unchecked for production-us-east-1. Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on repeated calls), so there is no error-rate, latency baseline or span-level corroboration, and no latency trend is inferred. Conclusion is partial: the cause is identified from exact log text, but the affected cluster has no metric, trace or Kubernetes coverage here, and the fault window boundaries and failure counts are unknown.

claims.text: The only index in this Elasticsearch source is app-262-prod-logs with 5 documents; it maps fields cluster, level, message, service and timestamp.
All 5 documents carry timestamps between 2026-11-23T15:32:53Z and 2026-11-23T17:02:53Z, and 3 of them are level ERROR with cluster 'production-us-east-1'.
In cluster production-us-east-1, service checkout-service logged ERROR 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (Stripe-US)' at 2026-11-23T15:32:53Z.

In cluster production-us-east-1, service payment-service logged ERROR 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms' at 2026-11-23T16:32:53Z — the payment service's own upstream call to stripe-us timed out after 30000 ms.
In cluster production-us-east-1, service checkout-service logged ERROR 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 44%)' at 2026-11-23T17:02:53Z.

The two non-error documents in the index ('Healthy: p95 latency 230ms' at 16:32:53Z and 'Healthy: success rate 99.7%' at 17:02:53Z, both for checkout-service) carry cluster 'production-eu-west-1'; they describe a different cluster than the US prod cluster and neither shows production-us-east-1 healthy nor provides a US baseline.

The US-prod checkout failures are caused by timeouts to the external payment provider stripe-us exceeding the 30s budget: payment-service's call to stripe-us /v1/charges hung 30s, checkout's payment provider response timed out, and checkout's payment-service circuit breaker then opened, shedding further PlaceOrder attempts. The evidence ends at the external provider; the log text does not say why stripe-us was slow or whether it returned an error.

In Kubernetes cluster `production` (namespace otel-demo), the checkout and payment deployments each report 1 replica available and 1 ready, and their pods checkout-6578865d87-v6flf and payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm are Running, ready, with restartCount 0 and startTime 2026-11-23T14:36Z (before the 15:32Z first error).

In cluster `production`, the checkout pod checkout-6578865d87-v6flf has no previous container instance (the previous-stream read was unavailable), and its current container log sample read 818 lines covering 2026-11-23T16:50:53Z–17:31:17Z in which the 200 newest lines are repeated successful 'payment went through (transaction_id: …)' and 'order confirmation email sent' records.

Feature-flag fault injection in cluster `production` was considered and rejected: the flagd-config ConfigMap declares paymentFailure (variants include '100%':1 … 'off':0) and paymentUnreachable, but every flag's defaultVariant is 'off', and the ConfigMap was applied once by helm at 2026-11-23T14:36:29Z (resourceVersion 512, single managedFields entry) with no evidence of a later change. It also belongs to cluster `production`, not to the production-us-east-1 cluster whose logs show the failures.

In cluster `production` at query time, the payment and checkout Services (ClusterIP, port 8080 → targetPort 8080) have populated Endpoints (10.244.0.11 for payment, 10.244.0.17 for checkout), and no NetworkPolicy or ResourceQuota objects exist, so there is no visible service/endpoint, network-policy or quota cause there.

Treat the external provider stripe-us as the first thing to check on production-us-east-1: its status/latency for /v1/charges around 2026-11-23T15:30–17:05Z, the credentials/routing/API base URL used by payment-service, and whether the 30s client timeout plus checkout's circuit-breaker thresholds (trip at a 44% failure rate) are appropriate; add payment-provider latency and error-rate series and a PlaceOrder error-ratio baseline so the next occurrence can be measured rather than inferred from log lines.

gaps: No metric data: every Prometheus call in this Run (get_label_values for service_name and k8s_cluster_name, execute_prometheus_instant_query on traces_span_metrics_calls_total, get_metric_names, list_prometheus_rules) returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so there is no error-rate, request-rate or latency series and no comparable baseline; no latency trend is inferred.

No trace data: traces_list_services and three traces_search calls returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so span-level attribution of the checkout/payment failures in production-us-east-1 is unknown and no call-edge or failure-rate conclusion can be drawn from traces.

No Kubernetes coverage of the affected cluster: Kubernetes access reads cluster `production` only, so pod status, container termination reasons, events, Services/Endpoints, ConfigMaps and any feature-flag state for production-us-east-1 are unknown; the healthy pod/log/flag findings in the claims describe cluster `production` (namespace otel-demo) and must not be transferred to production-us-east-1.

No Kubernetes events were available: the all-namespace event grouping query (kubernetes_jq_query kind=events) returned status no_data with zero items, so that query matched nothing and no Evicted, OOMKilled, BackOff, Failed, Unhealthy, SuccessfulCreate or SuccessfulDelete event can be cited for any pod in either cluster; pod-level restart/eviction evidence is therefore missing rather than absent.

Filtered pod-log reads returned nothing and are reported as unmatched queries only: a regex read of checkout-6578865d87-v6flf logs (err|error|fail|timeout|circuit|unavailable|declin|refus, 14:30–17:33Z) and one of payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm logs (same terms plus 'stripe', 549 lines read) both returned status no_data with zero matching lines; neither proves absence of errors in those pods. The full payment log read was also cut by a RESULT_TOO_LARGE error (48170 tokens over 200 lines), so its contents beyond the error-filter are unknown.

The checkout log view is incomplete by limit (81064c8c-567d-433d-bfeb-44ff896bc2e6-t0:30c0d303-d6ba-4b71-be6e-c17b7d926159 shows the newest 200 of 818 matching lines), so 618 earlier checkout lines in 14:30–17:33Z were not shown and are unknown.

The index holds only 5 documents: there is no log line between 15:32:53Z and 16:32:53Z, none before 15:32:53Z and none after 17:02:53Z, so when the incident began, whether it is still active, and how many requests failed are all unknown; the 44% figure comes only from the circuit-breaker message text.

The change_history integration is not integrated, so I cannot see whether any configuration, provider-route or credential change was applied to production-us-east-1 or to payment-service before 15:32:53Z; the only mechanism-level change evidence available is for cluster `production` (flagd-config applied once at 14:36:29Z).

The external dependency itself (stripe-us, the payment provider named in the log text) is outside the cluster and outside every available data source, so the trigger on the provider side — outage, throttling, network path or credential — is unknown.

Unverified downstream/customer impact: the log lines show failed checkout attempts and an open circuit breaker in production-us-east-1, but no order-volume, revenue or customer-facing evidence was available to quantify it.
next_steps: Check the stripe-us payment provider's own status/incident record and payment-service egress metrics for 2026-11-23T15:00–17:10Z on production-us-east-1.

Restore Prometheus and Jaeger reachability for this target so the checkout PlaceOrder error ratio (the existing CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh rule) and payment rpc_client_duration can be measured against a baseline.
If the goal is to rule out an injected fault in the affected cluster, obtain Kubernetes/flagd visibility for production-us-east-1 and read its flagd-config and pod states for the same window.

notes: This tool has no time range: it shows the cluster's indices and mappings at the moment of the query, which can be after the authorized window.
view.cannot_prove: This is the state at the moment of the query only: it cannot prove which indices, fields or document counts existed during the incident window, nor that any document lies in that window. A field that is mapped is not proof that documents carry it.

Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

data.alertmanager.yml:
global: {}
receivers:
- name: opspilot
  webhook_configs:
  - http_config:
      authorization:
        [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
        type: Bearer [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]: 0
    send_resolved: true
    url: http://opspilot-web:8080/intake/alertmanager
- name: opspilot-self
route:
  group_by:
  - alertname
  - namespace
  - service
  group_interval: 1m
  group_wait: 10s
  receiver: opspilot
  repeat_interval: 1h
  routes:
  - matchers:
    - opspilot_self="true"
    receiver: opspilot-self
templates: []

data.relay:
connectors:
  spanmetrics: {}
exporters:
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] basicauth/prometheus
    endpoint: http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/otlp
    tls:
      insecure: true
extensions:
  basicauth/prometheus:
    client_auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
      username: collector
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  - basicauth/prometheus
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - otlphttp/prometheus
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - redis
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - otlp
      - debug
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - periodic:
          exporter:
            otlp:
              endpoint: otel-collector:4318
              protocol: grpc
          interval: 10000
          timeout: 5000

data.alerting_rules.yml:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
